explanations.answer: Cities to live in with pasturelands
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend, cities with pasturelands around them. The LORD tells Moses to have Israel give them from the inheritance the people will possess (Numbers 35:2). The Levites get homes and room for their herds and flocks. That fits what the LORD said earlier, that the Levites would receive no inheritance among the Israelites (Numbers 18:23-24). So the other tribes share what they have, and the Levites aren't left out.

explanations.answer: A strip of land by the Great Sea
explanations.explanation: Beachfront property, friend? I love the confidence. But the LORD says nothing about a strip of coast here. He tells the tribes to give cities and pasturelands from their own inheritance (Numbers 35:2). I spent years in a junk drawer, so I'm not the one to judge anybody's real estate dreams.

I get the guess, since the LORD spoke to Moses on the plains of Moab, across from Jericho (Numbers 35:1). But no valley gets named for the Levites. The LORD commands the Israelites to give cities for the Levites to live in, with pasturelands around them, from the inheritance they will possess (Numbers 35:2). One big valley would be easier to hand over, but that's not the order. It's cities, taken from the tribes' own land.

Refuge is the word. These are cities where a manslayer may flee (Numbers 35:6). A refuge is a safe place to run to, and six of the Levites' cities get that job. That's a lot of responsibility for a city that also has to find room for cows.

Worship makes sense, friend. The Levites are the ones who perform the work of the Tent of Meeting (Numbers 18:23). But for these six cities, the LORD names a different purpose. They are appointed as cities of refuge, a place a manslayer may flee to (Numbers 35:6). So the word that fits the blank is refuge.

Gathering is close to a word that does show up later. An assembly appears in this passage, and the manslayer stands trial before it (Numbers 35:12). But the six cities themselves are called cities of refuge. That's the word the LORD uses in verse 6.

Not quite, friend. The LORD says the cities are given to the Levites in proportion to each tribe's inheritance: “more from a larger tribe and less from a smaller one.” (Numbers 35:8) So the numbers aren't equal. A bigger tribe gives more, and a smaller one gives less.

That's right. The text says the cities are given in proportion to each tribe's inheritance: “more from a larger tribe and less from a smaller one.” (Numbers 35:8) It's like everybody chipping in on the cookie order by how big their family is. Same rule for all, different amounts.

explanations.answer: Someone who kills a person by accident
explanations.explanation: Right. The LORD says the cities are “…so that a person who kills someone unintentionally may flee there.” (Numbers 35:11) These cities are for someone who never meant to take a life. It's a serious matter, and the LORD makes a place for it.

explanations.answer: Someone who kills a person on purpose
explanations.explanation: That's the opposite, friend. A refuge is for the person who kills someone unintentionally (Numbers 35:11). Later in this same passage, the murderer must surely be put to death (Numbers 35:16). So a city of refuge isn't a hideout for him.

explanations.answer: Someone who kills an enemy in battle
explanations.explanation: Battle never comes up in this part. The LORD says the cities are for “…a person who kills someone unintentionally…” (Numbers 35:11). So the one running is someone who never meant to do it. I'd stick with what the text says.

Yes, friend, the assembly. The city of refuge keeps the avenger from reaching the manslayer first. His case goes before the assembly, so nothing gets settled on the road (Numbers 35:12). The city is where he stays safe until then.
I can see why a king sounds right. But this verse names no king. It says the manslayer stands trial before the assembly (Numbers 35:12). Sometimes a Bible detail is simpler than we expect.

Good guess, friend, but prophets aren't named in this verse. The LORD says the manslayer stands trial before the assembly (Numbers 35:12). A few verses later, the congregation is the one told to judge between the slayer and the avenger of blood (Numbers 35:24). So the people are the ones doing the judging. I'd say that's a lot of responsibility for a crowd.

Not all six, friend. The LORD says, “Select three cities across the Jordan and three in the land of Canaan as cities of refuge.” (Numbers 35:14) So the six are split, three on each side of the river. That's half and half.
Right. Three cities of refuge are across the Jordan, and three are in the land of Canaan (Numbers 35:14). It's like putting three cookies on each side of the tray. Six cities, split evenly.

Yes, friend. The six cities serve “…as a refuge for the Israelites and for the foreigner or stranger among them…” (Numbers 35:15). Anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there. The door isn't only for one group.

Actually, the foreigner is included. The LORD says the six cities are “…a refuge for the Israelites and for the foreigner or stranger among them, so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there.” (Numbers 35:15) So it's open to the stranger too. That's a wide door.

explanations.answer: He must be put to death
explanations.explanation: That's what the LORD says. For each of these, iron, a stone of deadly size and a deadly object of wood, he says the one who killed is a murderer, and “the murderer must surely be put to death.” (Numbers 35:16-18) It's a heavy part of the passage. The LORD is clear about it.

explanations.answer: He must pay the family back
explanations.explanation: Paying back isn't the answer here. For the murderer, the LORD says, “the murderer must surely be put to death.” (Numbers 35:16) Later he also says not to accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who deserves to die (Numbers 35:31). So a payment doesn't change it.

explanations.answer: He must be sent out of the land
explanations.explanation: Being sent away isn't what the LORD says. In all three cases, iron, stone and wood, the murderer “…must surely be put to death.” (Numbers 35:16-18) The text doesn't mention sending him out of the land. It's a serious part, and the answer is plain.

Yes, that's what the text says. “The avenger of blood is to put the murderer to death; when he finds him, he is to kill him.” (Numbers 35:19) This is for the murderer, not for the one who killed by accident. That's why the difference matters so much in this passage.

The text says the opposite, friend. “The avenger of blood is to put the murderer to death; when he finds him, he is to kill him.” (Numbers 35:19) That's the murderer. The one who killed unintentionally has a city of refuge to run to.

Yes, even a bare hand can do it. The verses just before this one name an iron object, a stone and a wooden object (Numbers 35:16-18). Then verse 21 adds that if in hostility someone strikes another with his hand and he dies, the one who struck him must surely be put to death, and he is a murderer. So no tool is needed in that case. It's a heavy part, and the text is clear.

Careful here, friend. The earlier verses do list an iron object, a stone and wood (Numbers 35:16-18). But verse 21 goes on to say that if in hostility someone strikes another with his hand and he dies, he is a murderer who must surely be put to death. So a hand in hostility counts too. That makes this one True.

explanations.answer: Protect him from the avenger of blood
explanations.explanation: That's it, friend. When the killing was an accident, the assembly shields the manslayer from the avenger of blood (Numbers 35:25). Then the assembly brings him back to the city of refuge where he fled. He lives there until the death of the high priest.

explanations.answer: Hand him over to the avenger of blood
explanations.explanation: Other way around, friend. The avenger is the one the assembly guards him from, not the one it gives him to (Numbers 35:25). After that, the assembly sends him back to the city of refuge he fled to. It's a safe place, not a handoff.

explanations.answer: Make him pay the family a fine
explanations.explanation: No fine shows up in this part, friend. The assembly's job is to protect the manslayer from the hand of the avenger of blood, and then it returns him to the city of refuge (Numbers 35:25). Nothing about a payment. I'd keep the wallet closed on this one.

Death is the word. The manslayer “…must live there until the death of the high priest, who was anointed with the holy oil.” (Numbers 35:25) Only after that may he return to the land he owns (Numbers 35:28). He stays put until then.

That's close to something that sounds official, but no. The text says the manslayer must live in the city “…until the death of the high priest, who was anointed with the holy oil.” (Numbers 35:25) It's a death that ends the stay, not a word from him. Easy to mix up.

A blessing would be a nice way to leave, friend. But the text says the manslayer must live there “…until the death of the high priest, who was anointed with the holy oil.” (Numbers 35:25) So the word in the blank is death. After that, he may go back to his land (Numbers 35:28).

Not in this case, friend. If the avenger of blood finds the manslayer outside his city of refuge and kills him, “…then the avenger will not be guilty of bloodshed…” (Numbers 35:27) The manslayer must remain in his city until the high priest dies (Numbers 35:28). It's a serious rule, and it shows how much the city's limits matter.

That's right. The text says, “…then the avenger will not be guilty of bloodshed, because the manslayer must remain in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest.” (Numbers 35:27-28) The city is where he's protected. Outside it, that protection is gone.

Yes. The text says the murderer is put to death “…on the testimony of the witnesses. But no one is to be put to death based on the testimony of a lone witness.” (Numbers 35:30) One voice isn't enough for something this serious. It takes more than one.

One isn't enough, friend. The LORD says, “…no one is to be put to death based on the testimony of a lone witness.” (Numbers 35:30) It's on the testimony of the witnesses, more than one. That's a safeguard built right into the law.
Witnesses are required. The text says the murderer is put to death “…on the testimony of the witnesses.” (Numbers 35:30) And a lone witness doesn't count either. So it can't happen with none.

Right. The LORD says, “You are not to accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who deserves to die; he must surely be put to death.” (Numbers 35:31) No payment changes that. That's about as clear as the text gets.

explanations.answer: Accept it if the family agrees
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't leave room for that, friend. “You are not to accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who deserves to die; he must surely be put to death.” (Numbers 35:31) The family isn't mentioned as a way around it. The answer is no ransom.

explanations.answer: Accept it once a priest approves
explanations.explanation: A priest doesn't change it either. The LORD says, “You are not to accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who deserves to die; he must surely be put to death.” (Numbers 35:31) No approval is listed. The rule is plain.

Not so, friend. The LORD says, “Nor should you accept a ransom for the person who flees to a city of refuge and allow him to return and live on his own land before the death of the high priest.” (Numbers 35:32) No payment shortens the stay. He waits until the high priest dies.

That's right. The text says, “Nor should you accept a ransom for the person who flees to a city of refuge and allow him to return and live on his own land before the death of the high priest.” (Numbers 35:32) So no buying a ticket home early. It's the same rule as before, and it's firm.

Blood is the word. The text says, “…no atonement can be made for the land on which the blood is shed, except by the blood of the one who shed it.” (Numbers 35:33) It also says bloodshed pollutes the land. It's a weighty verse, and the answer is plain.

An offering is a natural thing to think of, friend. But the text names only one thing. “…no atonement can be made for the land on which the blood is shed, except by the blood of the one who shed it.” (Numbers 35:33) So the word is blood.

Prayer is a good thing, but it's not what this verse names. The text says, “…no atonement can be made for the land on which the blood is shed, except by the blood of the one who shed it.” (Numbers 35:33) So the blank is blood. I'd read that one slowly.

That's the reason the text gives. Then the LORD says, “Do not defile the land where you live and where I dwell. For I, the LORD, dwell among the Israelites.” (Numbers 35:34) The land matters because He lives among His people. Just before this, He says bloodshed pollutes the land (Numbers 35:33). I think that's a lot to take in, and it shows how seriously He treats life.

explanations.answer: Their crops will not grow there
explanations.explanation: Crops aren't the reason in this verse, friend. The LORD says, “Do not defile the land where you live and where I dwell. For I, the LORD, dwell among the Israelites.” (Numbers 35:34) The reason given is that He dwells among them. The text doesn't say anything about harvests here.

explanations.answer: Other nations will hear of it
explanations.explanation: Other nations aren't mentioned in this verse, friend. The LORD gives a different reason: “Do not defile the land where you live and where I dwell. For I, the LORD, dwell among the Israelites.” (Numbers 35:34) The reason is that He lives among His people there. That's what is at stake, and it isn't about what anyone else might hear.
